slides.0.title: Traditional-method sparkling wines of Europe
slides.0.subtitle: One method, four terroirs and four sets of rules
slides.1.title: Cava
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Varieties and region
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The traditional varieties are Macabeo, Xarel·lo and Parellada, with Chardonnay and Pinot Noir also permitted; most production is concentrated around Penedès in Catalonia
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Ageing tiers
slides.1.highlights.1.content: At least 9 months on the lees; Reserva 18 months, Gran Reserva 30 months, and Cava de Paraje Calificado (single site) 36 months
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The quality dispute and breakaways
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Cava has long been known for cheap volume exports; producers unhappy with the image have left: Raventós i Blanc in 2012, now labelling Conca del Riu Anoia, and Corpinnat’s nine members in 2019. Neither is an official DO
slides.1.content: Cava is the textbook case of scale versus quality image.
slides.2.title: Crémant and Franciacorta
slides.2.highlights.0.title: French Crémant
slides.2.highlights.0.content: France has eight Crémant AOCs: Alsace, Bourgogne, Loire, Bordeaux, Die, Jura, Limoux and Savoie; all traditional-method with at least 9 months on the lees, using local varieties at prices below Champagne
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Franciacorta
slides.2.highlights.1.content: A Lombardy DOCG (1995) based on Chardonnay, Pinot Nero and Pinot Bianco, with up to 10% of the local Erbamat; NV needs at least 18 months on the lees, Millesimato 30 and Riserva 60
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Satèn
slides.2.highlights.2.content: A special Franciacorta style: white grapes only, under 5 bar, Brut only, with a silky mousse
slides.2.content: Franciacorta’s ageing rules are longer than Champagne NV’s 15 months, one argument for its premium positioning.
slides.3.title: Trentodoc and comparisons
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Trento DOC
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Mountain traditional-method sparkling wine from Trentino (DOC 1993), mainly Chardonnay; altitude brings high acidity and freshness; NV at least 15 months, Millesimato 24, Riserva 36
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Axes of comparison
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Compare traditional-method wines on five axes: climate and how acidity is kept, varieties, minimum lees ageing, volume and price, and industry structure (large houses or small growers)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Use of “méthode champenoise”
slides.3.highlights.2.content: EU rules reserve “méthode champenoise” for Champagne; other regions must use terms such as méthode traditionnelle or metodo classico
slides.3.content: In comparisons do not write one paragraph per region: cover two or three regions on each axis.
